---
title: "Animal physiology"
---

The animal half connects structure, regulation and environmental adaptation.
Use mammals as a reference, then compare alternative solutions in other animal
groups. This is a first teaching draft following the proposed core course;
actual specimen sessions and assessment details still require the established
course material.

## A useful study rhythm

Begin with the biological question, read the connected tutorial and sketch the
mechanism. Use the slides for a short explanation or revision. Complete the
exercise tasks with units and labelled arrows, then answer the quiz before
opening its explanations. Revisit mistakes by repairing the mechanism rather
than memorising the right option.

The numerical examples are invented for teaching and can be completed by hand
or calculator. There is no required R component. Descriptive histology tasks
prepare observation and reasoning; they do not replace the actual tissue
collection, microscope work or anatomy practicals.

For integration, explain a whole-animal response using at least three units:
how is it sensed, how do effectors change, what fuels it, and what transport,
thermal and water costs follow? Continue with the [plant half](../plant/index.qmd)
and [practical work](../practicals/index.qmd).
